title: Open-unit-normalized base change on arbitrary constant strict towers
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For every scheme $X$ use its small pro-etale site with the chosen small skeleton, its constant ring sheaf $\underline B_X$, the abelian category of module sheaves, and $\mathcal T_X=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B_X))$ of strict inverse systems. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal T_X)$. Use the termwise inverse image $G_u$, total derived termwise direct image $R_u$, and exact open extension $J_j$ with their specified adjunctions and compositors [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations] [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. For a cartesian square with opens $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and maps $g:X'\to X$, $g_U:U'\to U$, the restriction/direct-image comparison $j^{-1}g_*\cong(g_U)_*j'^{-1}$ on module sheaves is identity on the same pulled-back sections. Its left-adjoint comparison induces a canonical isomorphism $\beta_{j,g}:G_gJ_j\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{j'}G_{g_U}$. Its inverse is exactly the $J_{j'}\dashv G_{j'}$ transpose of $G_{g_U}\eta_j$, followed by the canonical inverse-image square identification. This determines $\beta$ naturally, on sheaves, strict towers, complexes and their unbounded derived categories. For $h:X''\to X'$ and the corresponding opens, $\beta_{j,gh}=(\beta_{j',h}G_{g_U})\circ(G_h\beta_{j,g})$, inserting pullback compositors. For opens $j_1:U\hookrightarrow V$, $j_2:V\hookrightarrow X$, the comparison for $j_2j_1$ is $(J_{j_2'}\beta_{j_1,g_V})\circ(\beta_{j_2,g}J_{j_1})$ under open-composition identifications. Identity base changes and identity opens give identities under the specified unit identifications. All equations hold before evaluation. Evaluating at any index for finite $B$ gives the specified finite open base-change comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change].

proof.text: Use [lem-cbc-open-square-section-restriction-mate], proved in this module from [lem-cbc-tower-square-unit-sections], naturality and the triangle identity. The projection-preserving site-square identity relates the two restrictions along the site adjunction units. Invertibility follows independently from conjugation of the already constructed invertible open comparison of Step 2.

On module sheaves the specified restriction comparison is already the exchange mate by definition. The fixed-coefficient open comparison transports the fully faithful ordinary open extension to moduleJ, so the chosen open adjunction has invertible unit. moduleOpenSquare identifies the pulled-back open extension with one in the essential image of the new open extension; its counit is therefore invertible there. The counit formula for the adjunction transpose proves singleBetaInv invertible, hence openBetaModule_isIso. The iterated-mate identity identifies the conjugate comparison with openBetaModule; applying the open Hom equivalence to its inverse gives exactly the pulled-back open unit, proving openBetaModule_normalized.

Prove inverse-image square pasting from the conjugate compositor coherence. Apply horizontal and vertical mate-pasting to obtain the two module open-composition laws. For identity arrows the section-normalized direct-image unit laws give the inverse-image unit laws; transposing those laws gives the open identity comparisons. The private helpers reproduce these elementary calculations without importing the calculus module, which now consumes this item.

source.place: Tag 0B65, adjoint transformation; identity and conjugation laws for mates

proof.text: Apply the sheaf comparison and its inverse at every index of a strict tower. For a transition $a:M_{n+1}\to M_n$, naturality says $L_2(a)\beta_{M_{n+1}}=\beta_{M_n}L_1(a)$; hence these components form a tower map, and the same equation for $b$ proves they are inverse tower maps. On a complex of towers, naturality with respect to each differential is the chain-map equation. All equations of Steps 3-6 hold at every tower index and cochain degree, hence hold as equations of tower and chain maps. This is justified in the ordinary functor and complex categories before localization; equality of their morphisms is componentwise equality. The adjunction units are termwise by [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations] and [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension], so the chain maps retain the transpose normalization.

source.place: Tag 09AE, definition-extension-zero; explicit termwise tower and chain-map argument

proof.text: Use exact_mate_tower to descend the module inverse comparison and its unit equation before evaluation. The squareG_lift equation identifies the descended inverse-image square with the specified derived square. Injectivity of the chosen open adjunction Hom equivalence identifies this descended map with betaInv, proving openBetaNormalization. Apply evalD_square to the same termwise square and replace the evaluation comparisons by their specified aliases, proving openBetaEvaluation. The complex component equation follows directly from the termwise map definitions.

proof.text: The finite pullback comparison is the inverse mate of cDirect between equivalences, hence is invertible. The finite open comparison is the inverse mate of its inverse and is invertible for the same reason. Both chosen comparisons therefore retain the specified adjunction units.

source.place: Tag 09AE; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0GL1, open normalization refinement and its finite specialization

proof.text: For composable scheme arrows, compare the two direct-image presentation maps on sections after applying cUnderlying. The specifications of cDirect and moduleRComp, together with naturality of cUnderlying for sheaf maps and site restrictions, identify both paths with restriction along Over.pullbackComp.hom. Conjugate by the composite adjunctions: moduleGComp and upperStarComp are the corresponding left-adjoint compositors. Mate pasting gives finitePull_compSquare; transport the natural-transformation square along the commutativity relation and then take its components to obtain finitePull_square with moduleSquareG.inv and upperStarCompIso.hom. Take open mates. The ordinary open base-change map has mate upperStarCompIso.hom, whereas singleBetaInv has mate moduleSquareG.inv. The converse mate-cube theorem proves the ordinary open cube; cancel the two base-change isomorphisms to obtain its forward orientation. Apply the exact-functor cube localization theorem to the six specified faces. Its derived ordinary face is exactly ordinaryOpenExtensionBaseChangeIso, by equality of the defining conjugate isomorphisms. Thus openBetaFiniteCompatibility compares the actual maps on the full unbounded derived category, without evaluation detecting equality.
